missions.name: Westerplatte
missions.brief: 04:45, 1 September. The battleship Schleswig-Holstein, moored in the harbour channel, opens fire on the Polish Military Transit Depot. German marines and Danzig police blow a gap in the brick border wall and push through the woods toward the outposts, guardhouses and the barracks. 182 defenders hold out for seven days. Take the five positions in order.

missions.name: Mokra
missions.brief: 1 September, north of Kłobuck. The 4th Panzer Division attacks eastward across open, rolling fields into the Wołyńska Cavalry Brigade: uhlans dug in at both ends of the woods around Mokra, 37 mm Bofors anti-tank guns, 75 mm field guns firing over open sights, and the armoured train Śmiały on the north–south railway. The Germans lose dozens of tanks before the Poles withdraw after dark. Take the five positions in order.

missions.name: Battle of the Bzura
missions.brief: Night of 9 September. General Kutrzeba's Poznań Army strikes south across the Bzura between Łęczyca and Piątek into the thinly spread German 30th Infantry Division, the largest Polish counter-offensive of the campaign. Poles: force the river bridges and take the church hill at Góra Świętej Małgorzaty. Germans: hold the south bank until the clock runs out.

missions.name: Siege of Warsaw — Wola
missions.brief: 8 September. The 4th Panzer Division drives east along Wolska Street into the western suburbs of Warsaw. The 40th Infantry Regiment "Children of Lwów" waits behind barricades of carts and trams, with anti-tank guns at the church gate and barrels of turpentine from the Dobrolin works ready to set the street ablaze. Fight street by street and take the five positions in order.

missions.name: Starachowice Works
missions.brief: The munitions works of the Central Industrial Region, a showpiece of Polish rearmament, lie in the path of the German advance. Fight through the gate, the rail yard and the assembly halls, take the boiler house and storm the administration block before the plant is lost.

missions.name: Danzig Polish Post Office
missions.brief: Free City of Danzig, 04:45, 1 September. Danzig police and the SS Heimwehr storm the Polish Post Office on Heveliusplatz. About fifty postal workers and reservists with pistols, grenades and three light machine guns hold the building for fifteen hours: a feint at the front door, a breach through the wall of the neighbouring Work Office, field guns at 11:00, a demolition charge at 17:00 and finally petrol pumped into the cellar. Take the five positions in order.

missions.name: Modlin Fortress
missions.brief: 13–29 September. Founded by Napoleon in 1806 and rebuilt by the Russians as Novogeorgievsk, the fortress at the confluence of the Vistula and the Narew becomes the last refuge of the Modlin and Łódź Armies under General Thommée. Brick barracks, casemates and the arsenal ring the parade ground behind the gate. Break through the gate, clear the Long Barracks, seize the arsenal, storm the casemate battery and take the citadel command post.

missions.name: Test Range
missions.brief: Zero your rifle and learn the weapons: static targets at 10, 25, 50, 100 and 200 m, a walking target, and two tanks to test armour, crushing and the coaxial MG. Infinite ammunition.
